records.source: לְמַ֤עַן צִיּוֹן֙ לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה וּלְמַ֥עַן יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט עַד־יֵצֵ֤א כַנֹּ֨גַהּ֙ צִדְקָ֔הּ וִישׁוּעָתָ֖הּ כְּלַפִּ֥יד יִבְעָֽר׃
records.gloss: For [the] sake of Zion not I will be silent, and for [the] sake of Jerusalem not I will be quiet, until goes out like the brightness her righteousness, and her salvation like a torch [that] burns.
pieces: Because of Zion I will not be silent, \q and because of Jerusalem I will not keep still, \q until her righteousness breaks out like daybreak \q and her salvation burns like a torch.

L.1: For the sake of Zion I will not be silent, \q and for the sake of Jerusalem I will not be quiet, \q until her righteousness goes out like brightness, \q and her salvation like a torch [that] burns.

R.1: I will not stay silent for the sake of Zion. \q I will not keep quiet for the sake of Jerusalem. \q I will keep speaking until her righteousness shines out like the morning light, \q and her salvation blazes like a burning torch.

decisions.choice: I: the speaker is probably the prophet, the anointed one who spoke in 61:1-11; it may be the LORD
decisions.reason: Chapter 61 ends with the anointed speaker's song, and 62:1 continues in the first person. But God also says he has kept silent and will not keep silent (42:14; 57:11; 65:6), and in 62:6 the speaker appoints watchmen. The verse does not name the speaker.

decisions.choice: her righteousness: her being put right by God, her vindication, made visible to all
decisions.reason: Paired with salvation, righteousness here is the right standing God gives Zion when he rescues her, as in 46:13, 51:5 and 61:11. Verse 2 says the nations will see it.

decisions.choice: like brightness, like a burning torch: plain for everyone to see
decisions.reason: The light of dawn and a burning torch both shine out where all can see them; Zion's restoration will not be hidden (60:1-3).

records.heading: A new name for Zion

records.source: וְרָא֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ צִדְקֵ֔ךְ וְכָל־מְלָכִ֖ים כְּבוֹדֵ֑ךְ וְקֹ֤רָא לָךְ֙ שֵׁ֣ם חָדָ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁ֛ר פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִקֳּבֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: And will see nations your righteousness, and all kings your glory, and it will be called to you a name new which the mouth of Yahweh will designate it.
pieces: Nations will see your righteousness \q and every king your glory. \q You will be given a new name, \q one that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will pronounce with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own mouth.

L.2: And nations will see your righteousness, \q and all kings your glory; \q and you will be called [by] a new name \q which the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will designate.

R.2: The nations will see your righteousness, \q and all their kings will see your glory. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will speak a new name for you, \q and that is what you will be called.

decisions.choice: your, you: Zion herself, now addressed directly
decisions.reason: Verse 1 spoke about Zion; from here the speaker turns to her and speaks to her as a woman (feminine forms), as in 60:1-22.

decisions.choice: a new name: a new identity and standing, given by the LORD himself
decisions.reason: In the Bible a new name marks a new relationship or calling (Genesis 17:5; 32:29). Verses 4 and 12 give Zion's new names, and 65:15 promises God's servants another name; Revelation 2:17 and 3:12 take up the promise.

decisions.choice: designate: name exactly, pronounce
decisions.reason: The verb means to mark out or specify by name (Genesis 30:28; Numbers 1:17). The name is not one people invent but one God himself pronounces.

records.source: וְהָיִ֛יתְעֲטֶ֥רֶת תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת בְּיַד־יְהוָ֑ה וּצְנִ֥יף מְלוּכָ֖ה בְּכַף־אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: And you will be a crown of beauty in [the] hand of Yahweh, and a turban of royalty in [the] palm of your God.
pieces: You will be a beautiful crown held in the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q a king's turban resting in the palm of your God.

L.3: And you will be a crown of beauty in the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and a royal turban in the palm of your God.

R.3: You will be like a beautiful crown that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} holds in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand. \q You will be like a king's turban in the hand of your God.

decisions.choice: a crown in the hand of the LORD: Zion is God's treasured royal ornament, held and displayed by him
decisions.reason: A crown held in the hand is kept safe and shown with pride. In 28:5 the LORD is the crown of beauty for his people; here the image turns round, and Zion is his.

decisions.choice: a turban: the reading tradition (qere)
decisions.reason: The written text (ketiv) and the reading tradition (qere) spell this word differently. Both are the word for a turban or headband worn by a king or priest (compare 3:23; Zechariah 3:5), so the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: like a beautiful crown; like a king's turban
decisions.reason: Readable adds "like" so the picture is not read as Zion turning into an object.

records.source: לֹֽא־יֵאָמֵר֩ לָ֨ךְ ע֜וֹד עֲזוּבָ֗ה וּלְאַרְצֵךְ֙ לֹא־יֵאָמֵ֥ר עוֹד֙ שְׁמָמָ֔ה כִּ֣י לָ֗ךְ יִקָּרֵא֙ חֶפְצִי־בָ֔הּ וּלְאַרְצֵ֖ךְ בְּעוּלָ֑ה כִּֽי־חָפֵ֤ץ יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔ךְ וְאַרְצֵ֖ךְ תִּבָּעֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Not will it be said of you again, Abandoned, and of your land not will it be said again, Desolation; but to you it will be called, Hephzibah, and to your land, Beulah; for delights Yahweh in you, and your land will be married.
pieces: No one will call you Abandoned any longer, \q or call your land Desolation. \q Instead you will be named She Is My Delight, and your land Wedded, \q because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} delights in you, \q and your land will be taken as a bride.

L.4: It will no longer be said of you, Abandoned, \q and of your land it will no longer be said, Desolation; \q but you will be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah; \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} delights in you, \q and your land will be married.

R.4: People will not call you Abandoned anymore. \q They will not call your land Ruined. \q Your new name will be I Delight in Her, and your land will be called Married. \q That is because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is pleased with you, \q and your land will be like a married woman.

decisions.choice: Hephzibah means "my delight is in her"; Beulah means "married" (a woman who has a husband)
decisions.reason: The new names answer the old ones. Abandoned is a wife left by her husband (54:6; 60:15), and Desolation is a land left empty (49:19; 54:1). Now God delights in Zion, and her land is like a wife with a husband. Hephzibah was also the name of King Hezekiah's wife (2 Kings 21:1).

decisions.choice: married: the land will be possessed, lived in and fruitful, like a wife with a husband
decisions.reason: An abandoned wife had no one to protect or provide for her, and an empty land produced nothing. The verb for marry also means to become master or owner, so a married land is one that has people who care for it. Verse 5 develops the picture.

decisions.choice: Literal keeps the names Hephzibah and Beulah; Balanced and Readable translate them
alternatives: My Delight Is in Her, Married at every level
decisions.reason: The names carry the meaning of the verse, and the reader needs to hear them against Abandoned and Desolation. Literal shows them as names; Balanced and Readable say what they mean.

decisions.choice: your land will be like a married woman
decisions.reason: Readable turns the verb into a plain comparison so the picture is clear.

records.source: כִּֽי־יִבְעַ֤ל בָּחוּר֙ בְּתוּלָ֔ה יִבְעָל֖וּךְ בָּנָ֑יִךְ וּמְשׂ֤וֹשׂ חָתָן֙ עַל־כַּלָּ֔ה יָשִׂ֥ישׂ עָלַ֖יִךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: For marries a young man a young woman, will marry you your sons; and [with the] joy of a bridegroom over a bride will rejoice over you your God.
pieces: Your sons will take you \q as a young man takes a young woman in marriage; \q your God will be glad over you \q with a groom's joy over his bride.

L.5: For [as] a young man marries a young woman, \q your sons will marry you; \q and [with] the joy of a bridegroom over a bride \q your God will rejoice over you.

R.5: As a young man marries a young woman, \q your children will marry you. That is, they will make their home in you. \q And your God will be as happy with you as a groom is with his bride.

decisions.choice: your sons will marry you: Zion's own people will take possession of her and live in her
decisions.reason: The image is bold: Zion's returning children settle in her as a husband takes a wife, so she is no longer empty (49:20-21; 54:1-3). The same consonants could be read "your builder" (compare 49:17), which would make God the one who marries her, as in 54:5; the vowels of the received text read "your sons".

decisions.choice: the joy of a bridegroom over a bride: God's delight in his people
decisions.reason: The wedding picture continues from 61:10 and returns in 65:19 and Zephaniah 3:17, where God rejoices over his people with singing.

decisions.choice: That is, they will make their home in you.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the marriage picture, following the meaning decision on this phrase.

records.source: עַל־חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הִפְקַ֨דְתִּי֙ שֹֽׁמְרִ֔ים כָּל־הַיּ֧וֹם וְכָל־הַלַּ֛יְלָה תָּמִ֖יד לֹ֣א יֶחֱשׁ֑וּ הַמַּזְכִּרִים֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה אַל־דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: On your walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen; all the day and all the night continually not they will be silent. [You] who cause to remember Yahweh, no rest [be] to you,
pieces: I have stationed guards on your walls, Jerusalem; \q through the whole day and the whole night they will keep calling out, never silent. \q You who keep reminding {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q do not rest,

L.6: On your walls, Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen; \q all the day and all the night continually they will not be silent. \q You who remind {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q [take] no rest for yourselves,

R.6: Jerusalem, I have put guards on your walls. \q They will call out all day and all night, and they will never be quiet. \q You who pray to remind {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promises, \q do not rest.

decisions.choice: watchmen who remind the LORD: people who pray without stopping, calling God's promises to his mind
decisions.reason: The watchmen do not guard against enemies here; they speak to God. The word for those who remind is the title of the royal recorder (36:3), whose task was to bring matters before the king. Prophets are called watchmen in 52:8, 56:10 and Ezekiel 3:17.

decisions.choice: I have appointed: the same unnamed speaker as in verse 1
decisions.reason: Whether this is the LORD or the prophet, the speaker who will not be silent (verse 1) now sets others on the walls who will not be silent either.

decisions.choice: take no rest: the command continues into verse 7
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on: they are to give themselves no rest and give God no rest until he acts.

decisions.choice: who pray to remind the LORD of his promises
decisions.reason: Readable says what reminding God means here; verse 7 shows the prayers are for God to do what he has promised for Jerusalem.

records.source: וְאַֽל־תִּתְּנ֥וּ דֳמִ֖י ל֑וֹ עַד־יְכוֹנֵ֞ן וְעַד־יָשִׂ֧ים אֶת־יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֛ם תְּהִלָּ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: and do not give rest to him until he establishes, and until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.
pieces: and do not let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} rest either, \q until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made Jerusalem secure and made her a city the whole earth praises.

L.7: and do not give rest to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} establishes [her], and until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

R.7: Do not let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} rest either. \q Keep on praying until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes Jerusalem strong again and makes her a city that people all over the world praise.

decisions.choice: give him no rest: pray to God without letting up
decisions.reason: The bold picture is of people who keep asking until God acts. Jesus tells a parable with the same point in Luke 18:1-8.

decisions.choice: a praise: something praised, a city others speak of with praise
decisions.reason: Jerusalem will be the object of the nations' praise (61:11; Jeremiah 33:9; Zephaniah 3:19-20).

decisions.choice: Keep on praying
decisions.reason: Readable repeats what the watchmen do, from verse 6, since Readable starts a new sentence here.

records.source: נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְהוָ֛ה בִּֽימִינ֖וֹ וּבִזְר֣וֹעַ עֻזּ֑וֹ אִם־אֶתֵּן֩ אֶת־דְּגָנֵ֨ךְ ע֤וֹד מַֽאֲכָל֙ לְאֹ֣יְבַ֔יִךְ וְאִם־יִשְׁתּ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־נֵכָר֙ תִּֽירוֹשֵׁ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָגַ֖עַתְּ בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Has sworn Yahweh by his right hand and by [the] arm of his strength: If I will give your grain again [as] food to your enemies, and if will drink sons of foreignness your new wine for which you have labored,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has bound {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} by oath, by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strong arm: \q I will not let your enemies eat your grain any more, \q nor let outsiders drink the new wine you worked to make,

L.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has sworn by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand and by the arm of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength: \q [Surely] I will no longer give your grain [as] food for your enemies, \q and foreigners will not drink your new wine for which you labored,

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has made a serious promise, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has put all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power behind it. \q He said: I will not let your enemies eat your grain anymore. \q People from other lands will not drink the wine you worked hard to make.

decisions.choice: if I give ... if they drink: an oath form meaning "I will never again"
decisions.reason: In a Hebrew oath, "if I do this" leaves the curse on oneself unsaid and means "I will certainly not do it" (compare 14:24; Psalm 89:36).

decisions.choice: by his right hand and his strong arm: God pledges his own power
decisions.reason: People swear by something greater than themselves; God has nothing greater, so he swears by himself (45:23; Hebrews 6:13). His right hand and arm stand for his strength (40:10; 52:10).

decisions.choice: enemies eating the harvest: the old curse of invasion reversed
decisions.reason: Covenant curses warned that foreigners would eat what Israel had grown (Deuteronomy 28:33, 51; Judges 6:3-6). The promise is that this will not happen again.

decisions.choice: has made a serious promise, and he has put all his power behind it
decisions.reason: Readable explains what swearing by his right hand and arm means.

records.source: כִּ֤י מְאַסְפָיו֙ יֹאכְלֻ֔הוּ וְהִֽלְל֖וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וּֽמְקַבְּצָ֥יו יִשְׁתֻּ֖הוּ בְּחַצְר֥וֹת קָדְשִֽׁי׃ס
records.gloss: but [those] gathering it will eat it, and will praise Yahweh; and [those] collecting it will drink it in [the] courts of my holiness.
pieces: no, the ones who reaped the grain will eat it, praising {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and the ones who picked the grapes will drink the wine in the courtyards of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy house.

L.9: but those who gather it will eat it and praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and those who collect it will drink it in the courts of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holiness.

R.9: Instead, the people who harvest the grain will eat it, and they will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q The people who pick the grapes will drink the wine in the courtyards of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Temple.

decisions.choice: eating and drinking in the courts of the sanctuary: the harvest enjoyed at God's festivals
decisions.reason: The Law told Israel to eat the tithe of grain and wine in the place God chose, rejoicing before him (Deuteronomy 12:17-18; 14:22-26). Those who grew the food will now enjoy it in worship.

decisions.choice: my: the LORD is still speaking, finishing the oath begun in verse 8
decisions.reason: The courts are God's own holy courts in the temple.

decisions.choice: the grain, the grapes, the wine
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what is gathered and drunk, from verse 8, where Hebrew uses only "it".

records.source: עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים פַּנּ֖וּ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָעָ֑ם סֹ֣לּוּ סֹ֤לּוּ הַֽמְסִלָּה֙ סַקְּל֣וּ מֵאֶ֔בֶן הָרִ֥ימוּ נֵ֖ס עַל־הָעַמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Pass through, pass through in the gates; clear the way of the people; build up, build up the highway; clear [it] of stone[s]; lift up a signal flag over the peoples.
pieces: Through the gates, go through! \q Open a road for the people! \q Pile it up, pile up the highway, and pick out the stones! \q Lift a signal flag high over the peoples!

L.10: Pass through, pass through the gates; \q clear the way of the people; \q build up, build up the highway; clear [it] of stones; \q raise a signal flag over the peoples.

R.10: Go out through the city gates! \q Get a road ready for God's people to travel on. \q Build a highway, and clear away the stones. \q Put up a signal flag so the nations can see it.

decisions.choice: pass through the gates: probably Jerusalem's gates, going out to prepare the way for those returning
decisions.reason: The commands are plural, to people in the city. The gates may instead be those of Babylon, as the exiles are told to go out from there (48:20; 52:11). Either way, the road is for God's people coming home.

decisions.choice: clear the way, build up the highway, raise a signal flag: the road home announced in earlier chapters
decisions.reason: The words repeat 40:3 and 57:14 (build up, build up, clear the way) and 11:12 and 49:22, where a signal flag is raised to the nations to bring Israel's scattered people home.

decisions.choice: God's people
decisions.reason: Readable says whose people they are; the road is for Israel returning to Zion (verse 11).

records.heading: Open a road for the people

records.source: הִנֵּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה הִשְׁמִ֨יעַ֙ אֶל־קְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ אִמְרוּ֙ לְבַת־צִיּ֔וֹן הִנֵּ֥ה יִשְׁעֵ֖ךְ בָּ֑א הִנֵּ֤ה שְׂכָרוֹ֙ אִתּ֔וֹ וּפְעֻלָּת֖וֹ לְפָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Look, Yahweh has proclaimed to [the] end of the earth: Say to [the] daughter of Zion, Look, your salvation comes; look, his wages [are] with him, and his recompense before him.
pieces: See, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has announced to the farthest parts of the earth: \q Tell Daughter Zion, \q "Look, your salvation is coming! \q Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prize with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has won goes ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

L.11: Look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has proclaimed to the end of the earth: \q Say to the daughter of Zion, \q "Look, your salvation comes; \q look, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wages [are] with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} recompense [is] before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.11: Listen! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has announced this to the whole world: \q Tell the people of Zion, "Look! The one who saves you is coming. \q Look! He is bringing with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the reward {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has won. \q What {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has earned goes in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: your salvation comes; his reward is with him: salvation here is God himself coming to save
decisions.reason: Salvation is spoken of as a person who comes and brings a reward, so it stands for the LORD who saves. The Septuagint has "your Savior". The words about the reward repeat 40:10, where the Lord GOD comes with his reward; Revelation 22:12 takes them up.

decisions.choice: say to the daughter of Zion: the words Matthew 21:5 uses for Jesus' entry into Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Matthew joins these opening words to Zechariah 9:9, "your king is coming to you".

decisions.choice: wages and recompense: what God has won, the people he has rescued
alternatives: the reward he gives his people
decisions.reason: As in 40:10, the reward is what the victor brings back, here the redeemed people of verse 12.

decisions.choice: the people of Zion
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who "daughter of Zion" is: the people of the city.

decisions.choice: the one who saves you
decisions.reason: Readable follows the meaning decision that salvation here stands for God coming as Savior, since the next line says "he".

records.source: וְקָרְא֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם עַם־הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ גְּאוּלֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלָךְ֙ יִקָּרֵ֣א דְרוּשָׁ֔ה עִ֖יר לֹ֥א נֶעֱזָֽבָה׃ס
records.gloss: And they will call them the people of the holiness, [the] redeemed of Yahweh; and to you it will be called Sought-After, a city not abandoned.
pieces: They will be named The Holy People, Those {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} Has Redeemed, \q and you will be named Sought After, The City Not Abandoned.

L.12: And they will call them The Holy People, The Redeemed of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q and you will be called Sought After, A City Not Abandoned.

R.12: People will call them The Holy People and The People {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} Has Bought Back. \q And you, Jerusalem, will be called Sought After and The City Not Abandoned.

decisions.choice: Sought After: cared for and longed for, no longer neglected
decisions.reason: The word means sought out, looked after. It reverses the taunt of Jeremiah 30:17, "Zion, whom no one cares for" (the same verb).

decisions.choice: The Holy People, The Redeemed of the LORD: the titles of Israel at the exodus, given again
decisions.reason: Israel was called to be a holy nation (Exodus 19:6; Deuteronomy 7:6). The redeemed of the LORD return to Zion in 35:9-10 and 51:10-11. 1 Peter 2:9 applies the titles to the church.

decisions.choice: A City Not Abandoned: the answer to the old name Abandoned in verse 4
decisions.reason: The chapter ends by undoing the name it began to undo; the same verb is used.

decisions.choice: you, Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city addressed, since the verse moves from "them" (the people) to "you" (Zion).
